claim: T-REX is the only platform that interrogates with high spatiotemporal resolution individual PFR-specific LDE-modification in live cells and organisms.
source: Our laboratory established T-REX—the only platform that interrogates with high spatiotemporal resolution individual PFR-specific LDE-modification in live cells and organisms (Parvez et al., 2016; Long et al., 2017c; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Parvez et al., 2016; Long et al., 2017c) and reference to a figure.

claim: T-REX can probe consequences of on-target PFR-modification at an accurately-determined ligand/target-binding stoichiometry, ligand chemotype, and spatiotemporal context of target engagement.
source: T-REX can probe consequences of on-target PFR-modification, at an accurately-determined ligand/target-binding stoichiometry, ligand chemotype, and spatiotemporal context of target engagement.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the capabilities of T-REX, supported by the context of the technology description.

claim: Traditional bolus electrophile-dosing methods simultaneously modify many proteins and typically give readouts that cannot be clearly linked to labeling of specific protein(s).
source: These features contrast with traditional bolus electrophile-dosing methods, that simultaneously modify many proteins, and typically give readouts that cannot be clearly linked to labeling of specific protein(s), and are limited in assignment of individual ligand occupancy.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about traditional methods versus T-REX, based on established understanding of the limitations of bolus dosing.

claim: T-REX has shown that electrophile signaling on PFRs typically functions through phenotypically-dominant pathways, such as gain-of-function or dominant-negative signaling.
source: T-REX has shown that electrophile signaling on PFRs typically functions through phenotypically-dominant pathways, such as gain-of-function or dominant-negative signaling Parvez et al., 2018.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Parvez et al., 2018).

claim: Several PFRs discovered were not enzymes, opening a new dimension into how PFRs can function to orchestrate signal propagation.
source: Several PFRs discovered were not enzymes, opening a new dimension into how PFRs can function to orchestrate signal propagation.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from prior research, implying discovery through T-REX studies.

claim: Sensor residues within PFR-enzymes are surprisingly not essential for enzyme-activity, or even close to the active site.
source: Furthermore, sensor residues within PFR-enzymes are surprisingly not essential for enzyme-activity, or even close to the active site.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from prior research, indicating unexpected properties of PFR-enzymes.

claim: Understanding precision electrophile signaling is a new means to uncover novel pathway players and intersections.
source: We further demonstrated recently that understanding precision electrophile signaling is a new means to uncover novel pathway players Poganik et al., 2021 and intersections Long et al., 2017b, protein-targets Long et al., 2017c; Zhao et al., 2018; Surya et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2022; Poganik et al., 2019 and chemically actionable sites (Liu et al., 2020) not traditionally considered drug discovery fare (Long et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The Keap1/Nrf2-antioxidant response (AR) axis is one of the most venerable LDE-signal-responsive pathways.
source: One of the most venerable LDE-signal-responsive pathways is the Keap1/Nrf2-antioxidant response (AR) axis (Hayes and Dinkova-Kostova, 2014), wherein dimeric-Keap1 is both a cytosolic anchor and an essential component of the E3-ligase complex responsible for the degradation of the key AR-promoting transcription factor, Nrf2.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Hayes and Dinkova-Kostova, 2014) and is a statement of established knowledge.

claim: Dimeric-Keap1 is both a cytosolic anchor and an essential component of the E3-ligase complex responsible for the degradation of Nrf2.
source: One of the most venerable LDE-signal-responsive pathways is the Keap1/Nrf2-antioxidant response (AR) axis (Hayes and Dinkova-Kostova, 2014), wherein dimeric-Keap1 is both a cytosolic anchor and an essential component of the E3-ligase complex responsible for the degradation of the key AR-promoting transcription factor, Nrf2.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the function of Keap1, supported by a citation.

claim: Both functions of Keap1 serve to inhibit Nrf2.
source: Both functions of Keap1 serve to inhibit Nrf2.
evidence: This is a statement about the role of Keap1 in the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway, based on established understanding.

claim: When Keap1 is LDE-modified, Keap1 function is compromised and active Nrf2 accumulates, promoting AR.
source: When Keap1 is LDE-modified, Keap1 function is compromised and active Nrf2 accumulates, promoting AR.
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of AR activation, based on established understanding of the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway.

claim: Two main models have been proposed for Nrf2/AR-axis: inhibition of Nrf2 degradation through the formation of an abortive Nrf2-Keap1 complex and release of Nrf2 from Keap1.
source: Two main models have been proposed for Nrf2/AR-axis: inhibition of Nrf2 degradation through the formation of an abortive Nrf2-Keap1 complex Zhang and Chapman, 2020; and release of Nrf2 from Keap1 Kensler et al., 2007, causing inhibition of Keap1 and a boost in free Nrf2 concentrations.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Zhang and Chapman, 2020; Kensler et al., 2007).

claim: The Keap1/Nrf2 pathway is a primary target of some drugs in clinic, for example, the blockbuster multiple sclerosis drug, dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera).
source: The Keap1/Nrf2 pathway is a primary target of some drugs in clinic, for example, the blockbuster multiple sclerosis drug, dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera) (Poganik et al., 2021; Poganik and Aye, 2020; Cuadrado et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and reference to a figure showing the structure of dimethyl fumarate.

claim: Compounds causing release of Nrf2 from Keap1 are under investigation.
source: compounds causing release of Nrf2 from Keap1 are also under investigation Raghunath et al., 2019.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Raghunath et al., 2019).

claim: It was recently unambiguously shown that substoichiometric modification of Keap1-alone is sufficient to promote gain-of-function Nrf2/AR-signaling.
source: However, consistent with the pleiotropic nature of electrophiles, it was not until recently that it was unambiguously shown that substoichiometric modification of Keap1-alone is sufficient to promote gain-of-function Nrf2/AR- signaling (Parvez et al., 2016; Poganik et al., 2021; Long et al., 2017b; Parvez et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Experiments on the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway are typically conducted in cancer cells, which have undergone rewiring of their AR and other pathways that feedback with AR.
source: Experiments are typically conducted in cancer cells, which have undergone rewiring of their AR and other pathways that feedback with AR.
evidence: This is a statement about the typical experimental context for studying the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway, based on established knowledge.

claim: Aberrant Wnt-signaling proteins, often present in cancer cells, rewire the interaction between AR and Wnt signaling.
source: For instance, aberrant Wnt-signaling proteins, often present in cancer cells, rewire the interaction between AR and Wnt signaling (Long et al., 2017b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Long et al., 2017b).

claim: Mutation of several postulated electrophile-sensor residues within human Keap1 (hKeap1) did not ablate electrophile sensing and did not ablate pathway-activation upon hKeap1(mutant)-specific labeling.
source: However, we have often found that mutation of several postulated electrophile-sensor residues within human Keap1 (hKeap1), did not ablate electrophile sensing, and did not ablate pathway-activation upon hKeap1(mutant)-specific labeling (Parvez et al., 2016; Parvez et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: This work demonstrates a generalizable means to study on-target electrophile signaling along the druggable Keap1/Nrf2/AR-axis in zebrafish (Z-REX).
source: To avoid several of the above issues, we here demonstrate a generalizable means to study on-target electrophile signaling along the druggable Keap1/Nrf2/AR-axis in zebrafish (Z-REX) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a statement of the main contribution of the work, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The Keap1/Nrf2/AR-axis and consequent AR-mediated gene upregulation have been previously studied in zebrafish models, but only under bolus electrophile dosing.
source: The Keap1/Nrf2/AR-axis and consequent AR-mediated gene upregulation have been previously studied in zebrafish models, but only under bolus electrophile dosing.
evidence: This is a statement about prior research in zebrafish, indicating a gap that the current work addresses.

claim: Under Z-REX and under bolus dosing, AR-response is mounted in the fish tail: the head is recalcitrant to AR-upregulation.
source: Using Z-REX, we explore how different segments of the embryo respond to bolus LDE exposure vs. Z-REX-assisted on-target LDE-delivery in vivo. Intriguingly, under Z-REX and under bolus dosing, AR-response is mounted in the fish tail: the head is recalcitrant to AR-upregulation.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Targeted knockdown of different zebrafish paralogs of Keap1 (zKeap1) identified that zKeap1a and zKeap1b are both inhibitors of AR in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state.
source: Targeted knockdown of different zebrafish paralogs of Keap1 (zKeap1) identified that zKeap1a and zKeap1b are both inhibitors of AR in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state, but have functionally diverged in their response to electrophiles
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the knockdown experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: zKeap1b is permissive for electrophile-stimulated AR-upregulation similarly to hKeap1.
source: zKeap1b is permissive for electrophile-stimulated AR-upregulation similarly to hKeap1
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: zKeap1a is unresponsive to electrophile-stimulated AR-induction, even in the presence of equal amounts of Keap1b.
source: zKeap1a is unresponsive to electrophile-stimulated AR-induction, even in the presence of equal amounts of Keap1b.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The contrasted electrophile sensing/signaling between zKeap1a and zKeap1b paralogs was recapitulated in cell culture.
source: Such contrasted electrophile sensing/signaling between these paralogs was recapitulated in cell culture.
evidence: This is a statement indicating that findings from zebrafish were validated in a different experimental system.

claim: For some PFRs electrophile, signaling modalities are partially uncoupled from electrophile sensing.
source: These data collectively illuminate intricate on-target-modification-specific nuances of electrophile signaling. They further highlight that for some PFRs electrophile, signaling modalities are partially uncoupled from electrophile sensing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Halo-hKeap1 is functionally active in zebrafish.
source: We first demonstrated functionality of this fusion protein in fish.
evidence: This is a statement about a validation experiment performed in the manuscript.

claim: Following mRNA injection directly to the yolk sac at the 1–4 cell stage, the resulting expression of Halo-hKeap1 at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) was ubiquitous.
source: Following mRNA injection directly to the yolk sac at the 1–4 cell stage, the resulting expression of Halo-hKeap1 at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) was: (1) ubiquitous
evidence: This is a statement about the expression pattern of Halo-hKeap1 in zebrafish, based on experimental observation.

claim: Following mRNA injection directly to the yolk sac at the 1–4 cell stage, the resulting expression of Halo-hKeap1 at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) was similar to the overall level of the endogenous zKeap1.
source: Following mRNA injection directly to the yolk sac at the 1–4 cell stage, the resulting expression of Halo-hKeap1 at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) was: (1) ubiquitous, and (2) similar to the overall level of the endogenous zKeap1, since global Keap1-signal doubled in transgene-injected fish, relative to controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a statement about the expression level of Halo-hKeap1 in zebrafish, based on experimental observation and quantification shown in a figure.

claim: The Keap1-antibody detects hKeap1 with similar or higher efficiency to zKeap1a/b-paralogs-combined.
source: Note: our Keap1-antibody detects hKeap1 with similar or higher efficiency to zKeap1a/b-paralogs-combined (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a statement about the specificity of the antibody used, based on experimental validation shown in a figure.

claim: Halo-hKeap1 was functionally active as confirmed using two independent readouts (live-imaging and mRNA-analysis).
source: We next confirmed using two independent readouts (live-imaging and mRNA-analysis) that Halo-hKeap1 was functionally active.
evidence: This is a statement about the validation of Halo-hKeap1 functionality using multiple experimental approaches.

claim: A drop in overall basal AR and AR-driven genes was observed selectively in zebrafish injected with Halo-hKeap1 mRNA, compared to controls injected with Halo-mRNA alone.
source: In both instances, a drop in overall basal AR and AR-driven genes was observed selectively in zebrafish injected with Halo-hKeap1 mRNA, compared to controls injected with Halo-mRNA alone (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Ubiquitous Halo-hKeap1-expression led to AR-downregulation selectively in the tail.
source: We observed during these validations differential AR-responsivity between the head and tail of the fish. This intriguing disparity was first measured in Tg(gstp1:GFP) fish, wherein ubiquitous Halo-hKeap1-expression led to AR-downregulation selectively in the tail (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: This spatially-selective response was also observed in Halo-hKeap1-mRNA-injected Casper embryos using qRT-PCR, where the tail showed a more prominent attenuation in the AR-driven endogenous zebrafish genes, than the head.
source: This spatially-selective response was also observed in Halo-hKeap1-mRNA-injected Casper embryos using qRT-PCR, where the tail showed a more prominent attenuation in the AR-driven endogenous zebrafish genes, than the head (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: hKeap1 functions in zebrafish in a zNrf2-dependent manner.
source: To further demonstrate that hKeap1 functions in zebrafish in a zNrf2-dependent manner, we made use of the zNrf2a/b-MOs previously described by several independent laboratories Timme-Laragy et al., 2012; Kobayashi et al., 2002; Sant et al., 2017 and the resulting morphants in our hands also gave rise to the expected AR-suppression outcome in Tg(gstp1:GFP) fish tail (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; left panel, 1st vs. 2nd bars; and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by citations and reference to figures.

claim: Upon Halo-hKeap1 overexpression in zNrf2-depleted morphants, no further AR-suppression in the tail was noted.
source: Upon Halo-hKeap1 overexpression in these zNrf2-depleted morphants, no further AR-suppression in the tail was noted (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; left panel: 1st-2nd vs. 4th-5th bars).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: This epistasis is strong evidence that hKeap1 and zNrf2 reside on the same axis.
source: This epistasis is strong evidence that hKeap1 and zNrf2 reside on the same axis, as required by the current model of Keap1/Nrf2/AR-signaling (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, supported by reference to a figure illustrating the model.

claim: hKeap1-expression had no effect on AR in the head in fish treated with control morpholinos (MOs).
source: Furthermore, since hKeap1-expression had no effect on AR in the head in fish treated with control morpholinos (MOs) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; right panel: 1st vs. 4th bar), as well as in non-MO-treated reporter fish (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A: 3rd vs. 4th bar), there may be a dominant suppressor of AR in the head.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: There may be a dominant suppressor of AR in the head.
source: Furthermore, since hKeap1-expression had no effect on AR in the head in fish treated with control morpholinos (MOs) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; right panel: 1st vs. 4th bar), as well as in non-MO-treated reporter fish (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A: 3rd vs. 4th bar), there may be a dominant suppressor of AR in the head.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the data, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Levels of both zNrf2a and zNrf2b were overall higher in the tail than the head.
source: The qRT-PCR analysis (Figure 1C) revealed that levels of both zNrf2a and zNrf2b were overall higher in the tail than the head.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: zNrf2b was a minor contributor to both segments of the fish and was almost undetectable in the head.
source: zNrf2b was a minor contributor to both segments of the fish and was almost undetectable in the head.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: Levels of zKeap1a were overall similar in the head and the tail.
source: Levels of zKeap1a were overall similar in the head and the tail, but zKeap1b was overall slightly depleted in the tail.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: zKeap1b was overall slightly depleted in the tail.
source: Levels of zKeap1a were overall similar in the head and the tail, but zKeap1b was overall slightly depleted in the tail.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: In the tail, only depletion of both zKeap1-paralogs increased AR (single knockdown was not effective at modulating AR).
source: With these validations in hand, we naively expected zKeap1a-knockdown to increase AR. However, in the tail, only depletion of both zKeap1-paralogs increased AR (single knockdown was not effective at modulating AR) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the knockdown experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Loss of zKeap1b decreased AR in the head.
source: More strikingly still, loss of zKeap1b decreased AR in the head, but knockdown of both zKeap1-paralogs increased AR as expected.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the knockdown experiments.

claim: Knockdown of both zKeap1-paralogs increased AR in the head as expected.
source: More strikingly still, loss of zKeap1b decreased AR in the head, but knockdown of both zKeap1-paralogs increased AR as expected.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the knockdown experiments.

claim: These data indicate an intriguing, antagonistic interplay between the two zKeap1 alleles.
source: These data indicate an intriguing, antagonistic interplay between the two zKeap1 alleles.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the knockdown experiments.

claim: Knockdown of zNrf2a suppressed the tail's ability to mount AR in response to an electrophile challenge.
source: Consistent with a previous report on Nrf2a-defective fish Mills et al., 2020, knockdown of zNrf2a suppressed the tail's ability to mount AR in response to an electrophile challenge, whereas zNrf2b-knockdown led to a hyper-elevated AR-response in the tail (Figure 2B left panel).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by a citation and reference to a figure.

claim: zNrf2b-knockdown led to a hyper-elevated AR-response in the tail.
source: Consistent with a previous report on Nrf2a-defective fish Mills et al., 2020, knockdown of zNrf2a suppressed the tail's ability to mount AR in response to an electrophile challenge, whereas zNrf2b-knockdown led to a hyper-elevated AR-response in the tail (Figure 2B left panel).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by a citation and reference to a figure.

claim: Overall zNrf2b countermands electrophile-induced AR-upregulation.
source: From the data in the tail, it is likely that overall zNrf2b countermands electrophile-induced AR-upregulation, whereas zNrf2a functions in mounting AR in response to electrophile stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in the tail.

claim: zNrf2a functions in mounting AR in response to electrophile stimulation.
source: From the data in the tail, it is likely that overall zNrf2b countermands electrophile-induced AR-upregulation, whereas zNrf2a functions in mounting AR in response to electrophile stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in the tail.

claim: NE-treatment of zKeap1a-depleted fish led to elevated AR in both head and tail.
source: We found that NE-treatment of zKeap1a-depleted fish led to elevated AR in both head and tail (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The fact that zKeap1a-knockdown was sufficient to rescue response to electrophile treatment in cells expressing GFP in the head strongly implies that the presence of zKeap1a is responsible for 'the head's' recalcitrance to mounting AR, following electrophile treatment.
source: Nonetheless, the fact that zKeap1a-knockdown was sufficient to rescue response to electrophile treatment in cells expressing GFP in the head (Figure 2B, right panel) strongly implies that the presence of zKeap1a is responsible for 'the head's' recalcitrance to mounting AR, following electrophile treatment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: In zKeap1b-knockdown fish, electrophile treatment elicited lower-fold AR-upregulation selectively in the tail.
source: By contrast, in zKeap1b-knockdown fish, electrophile treatment elicited lower-fold AR-upregulation selectively in the tail (Figure 2B left panel).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: This effect could be rescued by injection of Keap1b mRNA.
source: This effect could be rescued by injection of Keap1b mRNA, even though these procedures had little effect on the basal AR in this region (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the rescue experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: In fish subjected to no knockdown, electrophile treatment resulted in little or no AR-upregulation (~1.1-fold) in the head, although the tail was responsive (~3.4-fold).
source: Note: in fish subjected to no knockdown, electrophile treatment resulted in little or no AR-upregulation (~1.1-fold) in the head, although the tail was responsive (~3.4-fold) (Figure 2B, 1st bars in both panels).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Overall ~3-fold increase in the magnitude of AR following electrophile stimulation has been reported by us and other laboratories in cultured cells and animals, using multiple orthogonal readouts.
source: Overall ~3-fold increase in the magnitude of AR following electrophile stimulation has been reported by us Parvez et al., 2016; Parvez et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2015; Long et al., 2018 and other laboratories Huang et al., 2012; Levonen et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2009; Zou et al., 2016; Kachadourian et al., 2011; Dev et al., 2015; Trott et al., 2008 in cultured cells and animals, using multiple orthogonal readouts including GFP- and luciferase-reporter assays and by western blot and qRT-PCR analyses assessing endogenous AR-driven genes.
evidence: This is a statement about the magnitude of AR upregulation, supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Electrophile treatment of zKeap1a/1b-double-knockdown fish also upregulated AR in both head and tail.
source: Electrophile treatment of zKeap1a/1b-double-knockdown fish also upregulated AR in both head and tail (Figure 2B, both panels), an observation that may be due to re-routing of electrophile response in these fish, or possibly hinting at a dominant-negative effect being at play.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Zebrafish Keap1 paralogs have been shown to form heterodimers post lysis and these paralogs can occur in the same tissues.
source: Notably, zebrafish Keap1 paralogs have been shown to form heterodimers post lysis and these paralogs can occur in the same tissues, indicating that particularly in some tissues, a heterodimer of zKeap1 paralogs could be formed Li et al., 2008.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of zebrafish Keap1 paralogs, supported by a citation.

claim: Our data and previous reports indicate that there is dominant-negative effect shown by one zKeap1-allele, but typical regulatory behavior shown by the other, at least under electrophile stimulation.
source: Overall, our data and previous reports Kobayashi et al., 2009 indicate that there is dominant-negative effect shown by one zKeap1-allele, but typical regulatory behavior shown by the other, at least under electrophile stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data and prior reports, supported by a citation.

claim: Z-REX-targeted hKeap1-modification resulted in 1.5-fold AR-upregulation (~40% of what we observed with NE-bolus dosing) in the tail 34 hr-post-fertilization (hpf), following light-exposure 30 hpf.
source: We found that Z-REX-targeted hKeap1-modification resulted in 1.5-fold AR-upregulation (~40% of what we observed with NE-bolus dosing) in the tail 34 hr-post-fertilization (hpf), following light-exposure 30 hpf (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the Z-REX experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The head was unresponsive to Z-REX-targeted hKeap1-modification.
source: The head was unresponsive.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the Z-REX experiments.

claim: Whole-fish treatment with HNE (25 µM) at 30 hpf, for 4 hr, elicited similar tail-specific AR-upregulation as was found under Z-REX.
source: Whole-fish treatment with HNE (25 µM) at 30 hpf, for 4 hr, elicited similar tail-specific AR-upregulation as was found under Z-REX (Figure 3A inset; the last two bars in left panel).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding comparing Z-REX and bolus dosing, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Representative genes associated with drug metabolism under control of Nrf2 (Gst-isoforms, Hmox1, and Abcb6) were activated to similar levels between Z-REX and bulk HNE-treatment.
source: Representative genes associated with drug metabolism under control of Nrf2 (Gst-isoforms, Hmox1, and Abcb6) were activated to similar levels between Z-REX and bulk HNE-treatment, and AR modulation was most prominent in the tail (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: AR modulation was most prominent in the tail.
source: Representative genes associated with drug metabolism under control of Nrf2 (Gst-isoforms, Hmox1, and Abcb6) were activated to similar levels between Z-REX and bulk HNE-treatment, and AR modulation was most prominent in the tail (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Bolus LDE-treatment yielded mixed responses in most cases.
source: By contrast, bolus LDE-treatment yielded mixed responses in most cases (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The P2A-integrated construct yielded little or no AR-upregulation upon Z-REX, compared to that achieved with Halo-•-hKeap1.
source: Similar to our previous cell-based data, the P2A-integrated construct yielded little or no AR-upregulation upon Z-REX, compared to that achieved with Halo-•-hKeap1, demonstrated by both IF-imaging of GFP-reporter upregulation (Figure 3D–E) and qRT-PCR analyses targeting 3 different endogenous AR-driven genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the P2A control experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Upon bolus exposure to Tecfidera, both fused and non-fused systems gave twofold AR-upregulation, particularly in the tail region.
source: Importantly, upon bolus exposure to Tecfidera (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), an approved pleiotropic electrophilic drug that stimulates AR as part of its pharmaceutical program Poganik et al., 2021; Poganik and Aye, 2020, both fused and non-fused systems gave twofold AR-upregulation, particularly in the tail region (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the Tecfidera control experiments, supported by citations and reference to figures.

claim: At the level of target labeling by Z-REX, the non-fused expression system strongly-diminished the extent of LDE-signal on hKeap1 compared to the fused construct.
source: Importantly, at the level of target labeling by Z-REX, we showed that the non-fused expression system strongly-diminished the extent of LDE-signal on hKeap1 compared to the fused construct (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the biotin pulldown experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Using the same enrichment protocol, we examined the extent of hKeap1 labeling subsequent to bolus HNE-treatment of embryos and unexpectedly found little discernable hKeap1-modifcation.
source: Using the same enrichment protocol, we examined the extent of hKeap1 labeling subsequent to bolus HNE-treatment of embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 4). We unexpectedly found little discernable hKeap1-modifcation.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the biotin pulldown experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: This result is surprising because bolus dosing promoted AR-upregulation to a level similar to that elicited by Z-REX targeted hKeap1-HNEylation.
source: This result is surprising because bolus dosing promoted AR-upregulation to a level similar to that elicited by Z-REX targeted hKeap1-HNEylation (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is a statement about the surprising nature of the finding, supported by reference to figures.

claim: AR increased as the fish aged, such that the DMSO-treated group had significantly higher AR 48 hpf than 34 hpf.
source: AR increased as the fish aged, such that the DMSO-treated group had significantly higher AR 48 hpf than 34 hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A-B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the time course experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Z-REX gave a transient AR-upregulation, which peaked around 4 hr ple but returned to basal levels 8 hr ple.
source: Interestingly, Z-REX gave a transient AR-upregulation, which peaked around 4 hr ple but returned to basal levels 8 hr ple (Figure 3—figure supplement 5D).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the time course experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: When we examined the effects of bolus HNE-treatment, a similar kinetic profile was observed.
source: Conversely, when we examined the effects of bolus HNE-treatment, a similar kinetic profile was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 5E), although fish were constantly exposed to electrophile.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the time course experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Using Tg(gstp1:GFP) fish, we found that HDE, NE, and DE elicited similar AR-upregulation in fish tails upon Z-REX.
source: Using Tg(gstp1:GFP) fish, we found that these LDEs elicited similar AR-upregulation in fish tails upon Z-REX (Figure 4A), but the head was not responsive (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the Z-REX experiments with different LDEs, supported by reference to figures.

claim: The head was not responsive to HDE, NE, and DE upon Z-REX.
source: Using Tg(gstp1:GFP) fish, we found that these LDEs elicited similar AR-upregulation in fish tails upon Z-REX (Figure 4A), but the head was not responsive (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the Z-REX experiments with different LDEs, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Independent qRT-PCR analysis of endogenous AR-driven genes following Z-REX in casper fish gave broadly-consistent results across all the LDEs examined.
source: Independent qRT-PCR analysis of endogenous AR-driven genes following Z-REX in casper fish gave broadly-consistent results across all the LDEs examined (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Using Click-biotin-pulldown following Z-REX in vivo, we validated using DE as an example that hKeap1-labeling extent was similar to that achieved with HNE.
source: Using Click-biotin-pulldown following Z-REX in vivo, we validated using DE as an example that hKeap1-labeling extent was similar to that achieved with HNE (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the biotin pulldown experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Bolus dosing with HDE, NE, and DE elicited widely different AR that was chemical-structure dependent.
source: Having established that each LDE when targeted specifically to Keap1 could trigger tail-specific AR-upregulation, we compared effects on AR from whole-fish-LDE-exposure under otherwise identical conditions/timescales to Z-REX. Bolus dosing with these LDEs elicited widely different AR that was chemical-structure dependent.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments.

claim: By both imaging of the AR-reporter fish and qRT-PCR analysis of endogenous AR-driven genes, LDEs that did not contain a 4-hydroxyl group were best at eliciting AR.
source: By both imaging of the AR-reporter fish (Figure 5A–B) and qRT-PCR analysis of endogenous AR-driven genes (Figure 5C), LDEs that did not contain a 4-hydroxyl group were best at eliciting AR.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: 4-dehydroxy species are intrinsically less electrophilic than their 4-hydroxylated counterparts.
source: Interestingly, 4-dehydroxy species are intrinsically less electrophilic than their 4-hydroxylated counterparts.
evidence: This is a statement about the chemical properties of the LDEs, based on established knowledge.

claim: Tecfidera gave outputs between those elicited by bolus HNE and NE (and of higher magnitude than the Z-REX responses).
source: Tecfidera gave outputs between those elicited by bolus HNE and NE (and of higher magnitude than the Z-REX responses) (Figure 5A–B; Cf. Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments with Tecfidera, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Bardoxolone methyl (CDDO-Me) was severely toxic to the fish at this concentration, although AR was upregulated.
source: Bardoxolone methyl (CDDO-Me; Phase II trials recently completed for pulmonary hypertension, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) was severely toxic to the fish at this concentration, although AR was upregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments with CDDO-Me, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Sulforaphane did not elicit AR under these conditions.
source: Sulforaphane (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) did not elicit AR under these conditions (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments with sulforaphane, supported by reference to figures.

claim: Regardless of the magnitude of the output in the tail, where responses were observed, there remained minimal, and indeed non-statistically-significant, increase in AR in the head.
source: However, regardless of the magnitude of the output in the tail, where responses were observed, there remained minimal, and indeed non-statistically-significant, increase in AR in the head (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the bolus dosing experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The trend of proteome labeling closely mirrored that of AR-upregulation elicited upon bolus dosing, with hydroxyl-bearing LDEs (HNE and HDE) manifesting a reduced level of proteome labeling and corresponding reduced AR-induction.
source: Interestingly, this trend closely mirrored that of AR-upregulation elicited upon bolus dosing, with hydroxyl-bearing LDEs (HNE and HDE) manifesting a reduced level of proteome labeling and corresponding reduced AR-induction (Figure 5 vs. Figure 6A-B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the proteome labeling experiments, supported by reference to figures.

claim: AR-upregulation upon bulk LDE-exposure is dominated by permeation/pharmacokinetic-effects over inherent ligand electrophilicity.
source: Thus, AR-upregulation upon bulk LDE-exposure is dominated by permeation/pharmacokinetic-effects over inherent ligand electrophilicity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the proteome labeling and AR-upregulation data.

claim: The divergent AR-induction in the front and hind portions of the fish was retained.
source: However, the divergent AR-induction in the front and hind portions of the fish was retained.
evidence: This is a statement about the consistency of the head vs. tail difference across different experimental conditions.

claim: We identified C273 (human numbering) as a candidate residue; the analogous residue in zKeap1a is an isoleucine, but it remains a cysteine in zKeap1b.
source: Based on this logic (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), we identified C273 (human numbering); the analogous residue in zKeap1a is an isoleucine, but it remains a cysteine in zKeap1b (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the phylogenetic analysis, supported by reference to figures.

claim: The C273I mutation has already been identified as a loss-of-function mutation to hKeap1.
source: This mutation has already been identified as a loss-of-function mutation to hKeap1 (Levonen et al., 2004; Saito et al., 2016), although it has not been extensively characterized, particularly in terms of how it interacts with wild-type(wt)-hKeap1.
evidence: This is a statement about prior knowledge of the C273I mutation, supported by citations.

claim: All four proteins sensed HNE equally well.
source: Intriguingly, all four proteins sensed HNE equally well (Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B-C).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the T-REX experiments in cells, supported by reference to figures.

claim: hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I) sensed NE marginally better than zKeap1a/b, both of which sensed NE to the same extent.
source: hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I) sensed NE marginally better than zKeap1a/b, both of which sensed NE to the same extent (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the T-REX experiments in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Differences in sensing abilities of the different proteins cannot explain the data we, and indeed others, have observed with zKeap1a and zKeap1b.
source: Thus, differences in sensing abilities of the different proteins cannot explain the data we, and indeed others, have observed with zKeap1a and zKeap1b.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the T-REX experiments in cells.

claim: All zKeap1a/b and hKeap1 could all significantly suppress AR.
source: We found that all zKeap1a/b and hKeap1 could all significantly suppress AR, again consistent with previous reports Li et al., 2008.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by a citation.

claim: zKeap1b appeared to be less efficient at suppressing basal AR than zKeap1a.
source: zKeap1b appeared to be less efficient at suppressing basal AR than zKeap1a (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: hKeap1(C273I) suppressed basal AR, but marginally.
source: hKeap1(C273I) suppressed basal AR, but marginally (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: None of these conditions were able to suppress basal AR to undetectable levels.
source: Critically, none of these conditions were able to suppress basal AR to undetectable levels (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: When zKeap1b was co-transfected with sub-saturating amounts of zKeap1a, no decrease in basal AR was observed relative to zKeap1a alone.
source: Intriguingly, when zKeap1b was co-transfected with sub-saturating amounts of zKeap1a, no decrease in basal AR was observed relative to zKeap1a alone (Figure 7D), implying that zKeap1a somehow affects the ability of zKeap1b to suppress AR.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: zKeap1a somehow affects the ability of zKeap1b to suppress AR.
source: Intriguingly, when zKeap1b was co-transfected with sub-saturating amounts of zKeap1a, no decrease in basal AR was observed relative to zKeap1a alone (Figure 7D), implying that zKeap1a somehow affects the ability of zKeap1b to suppress AR.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: When we performed similar experiments mixing hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I), a similar effect was observed.
source: When we performed similar experiments mixing hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I), a similar effect was observed (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: hKEAP1 and zKeap1b were significantly responsive to bolus NE treatment, significantly upregulating AR.
source: Intriguingly, although hKEAP1 and zKeap1b were significantly responsive to bolus NE treatment, significantly upregulating AR, zKeap1a, and hKeap1(C273I) were much less responsive (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells following NE treatment, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: zKeap1a and hKeap1(C273I) were much less responsive to bolus NE treatment.
source: Intriguingly, although hKEAP1 and zKeap1b were significantly responsive to bolus NE treatment, significantly upregulating AR, zKeap1a, and hKeap1(C273I) were much less responsive (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells following NE treatment, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: These data fully recapitulate data from zebrafish embryos expressing zKeap1a and zKeap1b.
source: In terms of AR-upregulation ability, these data fully recapitulate data from zebrafish embryos expressing zKeap1a and zKeap1b Kobayashi et al., 2009.
evidence: This is a statement about the consistency of the cell culture data with prior zebrafish data, supported by a citation.

claim: The C273I mutation is a likely cause of the zKeap1a's inability to mount AR.
source: These data further imply that the C273I mutation is a likely cause of the zKeap1a's inability to mount AR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell culture data.

claim: NE caused zKeap1b-alone-expressing cells to induce AR significantly, whereas zKeap1a-alone or zKeap1a/Keap1b-expressing cells mounted AR significantly less efficiently upon NE treatment.
source: Consistent with a dominant-negative effect on AR induction, NE caused zKeap1b-alone-expressing cells to induce AR significantly, whereas zKeap1a-alone or zKeap1a/Keap1b-expressing cells mounted AR significantly less efficiently upon NE treatment (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells following NE treatment, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: A similar effect was observed when hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I) were mixed.
source: A similar effect was observed when hKeap1 and hKeap1(C273I) were mixed.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the AR reporter assays in cells following NE treatment.

claim: These data explain why morpholinos targeting zKeap1a led to upregulation of electrophile-induced AR in both tail and especially the head and provide evidence for dominant-negative effects during Keap1/AR signaling.
source: These data explain why morpholinos targeting zKeap1a led to upregulation of electrophile-induced AR in both tail and especially the head and provide evidence for dominant-negative effects during Keap1/AR signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell culture data and the zebrafish data.

claim: zKeap1b accumulated Nrf2 in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state.
source: We found that zKeap1b accumulated Nrf2 in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state, whereas relative to zKeap1b, zKeap1a accumulated less Nrf2, and zKeap1a/zKeap1b accumulated an amount of Nrf2 that was significantly more than Keap1a alone and less than zKeap1b alone (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Relative to zKeap1b, zKeap1a accumulated less Nrf2.
source: We found that zKeap1b accumulated Nrf2 in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state, whereas relative to zKeap1b, zKeap1a accumulated less Nrf2, and zKeap1a/zKeap1b accumulated an amount of Nrf2 that was significantly more than Keap1a alone and less than zKeap1b alone (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: zKeap1a/zKeap1b accumulated an amount of Nrf2 that was significantly more than Keap1a alone and less than zKeap1b alone.
source: We found that zKeap1b accumulated Nrf2 in the basal (i.e. non-electrophile-stimulated) state, whereas relative to zKeap1b, zKeap1a accumulated less Nrf2, and zKeap1a/zKeap1b accumulated an amount of Nrf2 that was significantly more than Keap1a alone and less than zKeap1b alone (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments, supported by reference to a figure.

claim: When treated with NE, zKeap1b-bound Nrf2 was diminished by approximately 40%.
source: When treated with NE, zKeap1b-bound Nrf2 was diminished by approximately 40% (Figure 8A–B).
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments following NE treatment, supported by reference to figures.

claim: For zKeap1a and zKeap1a/zKeap1b no release of Nrf2 was observed upon NE treatment.
source: Conversely for zKeap1a and zKeap1a/zKeap1b no release of Nrf2 was observed.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments following NE treatment.

claim: These data agree with the paralog-specific regulation of electrophile signaling observed above, which showed that zKeap1a and the heterozygotic state were unable to upregulate AR effectively following electrophile treatment.
source: These data agree with the paralog-specific regulation of electrophile signaling observed above, which showed that zKeap1a and the heterozygotic state were unable to upregulate AR effectively following electrophile treatment.
evidence: This is a statement about the consistency of the immunoprecipitation data with the AR reporter data.

claim: Electrophile engagement of zKeap1b can trigger AR through causing net release of Nrf2.
source: Furthermore, given that significant amount of Nrf2 is bound to zKeap1b in both the heterozygous- and zKeap1b-only-expressing states, these data are consistent with a model in which electrophile engagement of zKeap1b can trigger AR through causing net release of Nrf2
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: zKeap1a (either with or without zKeap1b) cannot lead to net release of Nrf2 upon electrophile labeling, and hence cannot upregulate AR.
source: whereas zKeap1a (either with or without zKeap1b) cannot lead to net release of Nrf2 upon electrophile labeling, and hence cannot upregulate AR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: zKeap1a (either electrophile modified or unmodified) acts to suppress loss of Nrf2 binding to zKeap1b.
source: Thus, zKeap1a (either electrophile modified or unmodified) acts to suppress loss of Nrf2 binding to zKeap1b.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: zKeap1a exerts a significant direct effect on how zKeap1b responds to electrophiles.
source: Thus, zKeap1a exerts a significant direct effect on how zKeap1b responds to electrophiles, and hence the heterodimer, or higher order state(s) containing both proteins, must be a significant component of the zKeap1 present in the assay.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The heterodimer, or higher order state(s) containing both proteins, must be a significant component of the zKeap1 present in the assay.
source: Thus, zKeap1a exerts a significant direct effect on how zKeap1b responds to electrophiles, and hence the heterodimer, or higher order state(s) containing both proteins, must be a significant component of the zKeap1 present in the assay.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.
